arxiv-2204-13977.creator: Sivasankar M, Rama R
arxiv-2204-13977.description: Abstract If x x is a non-empty string then the repetition x ​ x xx is called a tandem repeat. Similarly, a tandem in a two dimensional array X X is a configuration consisting of a same primitive block W W that touch each other with one side or corner.

arxiv-2211-07718.title: Time-Dependent Hamiltonian Reconstruction using Continuous Weak Measurements
arxiv-2211-07718.creator: Karthik Siva, Gerwin Koolstra, John Steinmetz, William P. Livingston, Debmalya Das, L. Chen, J.M. Kreikebaum, N. J. Stevenson, C. Jünger, D. I. Santiago, I. Siddiqi, A. N. Jordan
arxiv-2211-07718.description: Abstract Reconstructing the Hamiltonian of a quantum system is an essential task for characterizing and certifying quantum processors and simulators. Existing techniques either rely on projective measurements of the system before and after coherent time evolution and do not explicitly reconstruct the full time-dependent Hamiltonian or interrupt evolution for tomography.

arxiv-2312-04601.title: Weak Supervision Performance Evaluation via Partial Identification
arxiv-2312-04601.creator: Felipe Maia Polo, Subha Maity, Mikhail Yurochkin, Moulinath Banerjee, Yuekai Sun
arxiv-2312-04601.description: Abstract Programmatic Weak Supervision (PWS) enables supervised model training without direct access to ground truth labels, utilizing weak labels from heuristics, crowdsourcing, or pre-trained models. However, the absence of ground truth complicates model evaluation, as traditional metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall cannot be directly calculated.

arxiv-2401-00246.title: Boosting Large Language Model for Speech Synthesis: An Empirical Study
arxiv-2401-00246.creator: Hongkun Hao, Long Zhou, Shujie Liu, Jinyu Li, Shujie Hu, Rui Wang, Furu Wei
arxiv-2401-00246.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have made significant advancements in natural language processing and are concurrently extending the language ability to other modalities, such as speech and vision. Nevertheless, most of the previous work focuses on prompting LLMs with perception abilities like auditory comprehension, and the effective approach for augmenting LLMs with speech synthesis capabilities remains ambiguous.

arxiv-2401-01054.title: Elastic Multi-Gradient Descent for Parallel Continual Learning
arxiv-2401-01054.creator: Fan Lyu, Wei Feng, Yuepan Li, Qing SunFanhua Shang, , Liang Wan, , Liang Wang
arxiv-2401-01054.description: Abstract The goal of Continual Learning (CL) is to continuously learn from new data streams and accomplish the corresponding tasks. Previously studied CL assumes that data are given in sequence nose-to-tail for different tasks, thus indeed belonging to Serial Continual Learning (SCL).

arxiv-2405-16308.title: n-th Root Optimal Rational Approximants to Functions with Polar Singular Set Thanks: The research of the last author was supported in part by a grant from the Simons Foundation, CGM-706591.
arxiv-2405-16308.creator: Laurent Baratchart, Herbert Stahl†, Maxim Yattselev
arxiv-2405-16308.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Laurent Baratchart, Herbert Stahl†, Maxim Yattselev. Let D D be a bounded Jordan domain and A A be its complement on the Riemann sphere. We investigate the n n -th root asymptotic behavior in D D of best rational approximants, in the uniform norm on A A , to functions holomorphic on A A having a multi-valued continuation to quasi every point of D D with finitely many branches.

arxiv-2504-12256.title: FLIP Reasoning Challenge
arxiv-2504-12256.creator: Andreas Plesner, Turlan Kuzhagaliyev, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2504-12256.description: Abstract Over the past years, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have demonstrated how AI can solve many perception and generation tasks, such as image classification and text writing, yet reasoning remains a challenge. This paper introduces the FLIP dataset, a benchmark for evaluating AI reasoning capabilities based on human verification tasks on the Idena blockchain.

arxiv-2504-19622.title: From Evidence to Belief: A Bayesian Epistemology Approach to Language Models
arxiv-2504-19622.creator: Minsu Kim, Sangryul Kim, James Thorne
arxiv-2504-19622.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Minsu Kim, Sangryul Kim, James Thorne. This paper investigates the knowledge of language models from the perspective of Bayesian epistemology. We explore how language models adjust their confidence and responses when presented with evidence with varying levels of informativeness and reliability. To study these properties, we create a dataset with various types of evidence and analyze language models’ responses and confidence using verbalized confidence, token probability, and sampling.

arxiv-2506-00983.title: Bridging the Gap: From Ad-hoc to Proactive Search in Conversations Conference: Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 13–18, 2025; Padua, Italy Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and De
arxiv-2506-00983.creator: Chuan Meng, Francesco Tonolini, Fengran Mo, Nikolaos Aletras, Emine Yilmaz, Gabriella Kazai
arxiv-2506-00983.description: Abstract . Proactive search in conversations (PSC) aims to reduce user effort in formulating explicit queries by proactively retrieving useful relevant information given conversational context. Previous work in PSC either directly uses this context as input to off-the-shelf ad-hoc retrievers or further fine-tunes them on PSC data.

arxiv-2507-02306.description: Abstract . Usability evaluation is crucial in human-centered design but can be costly, requiring expert time and user compensation. In this work, we developed a method for synthetic heuristic evaluation using multimodal LLMs’ ability to analyze images and provide design feedback.

arxiv-2510-27299.title: SHIFTED DOUBLE POISSON STRUCTURES AND NONCOMMUTATIVE POISSON EXTENSIONS
arxiv-2510-27299.creator: Leilei Liu, Jieheng Zeng, Hu Zhao
arxiv-2510-27299.description: Abstract . We develop a theory of noncommutative Poisson extensions. For an augmented dg algebra A A , we show that any shifted double Poisson bracket on A A induces a graded Lie algebra structure on the reduced cyclic homology. Under the Kontsevich–Rosenberg principle, we further prove that the noncommutative Poisson extension is compatible with noncommutative Hamiltonian reduction.

arxiv-2511-04785.title: BayesChange: an R package for Bayesian Change Point Analysis
arxiv-2511-04785.creator: Luca Danese, Riccardo Corradin, Andrea Ongaro
arxiv-2511-04785.description: Abstract We introduce BayesChange , a computationally efficient R package, built on C++ , for Bayesian change point detection and clustering of observations sharing common change points. While many R packages exist for change point analysis, BayesChange offers methods not currently available elsewhere.

pmc-10753866.creator: Juanjuan Zhang, Zhen Guo, Zhiming Wang, Weiming Zhu, Qiurong Li
pmc-10753866.description: IntroductionMicroRNA‐223 (miR‐223) has emerged as a promising noninvasive biomarker for Crohn's disease (CD). However, it is unclear which tissue derived miRNA‐223 can more accurately estimate CD disease activity.Materials and MethodsTo collect serum, terminal ileal mucosa biopsy and fecal samples from CD patients and healthy controls.

pmc-11648666.title: Social dilemma of nonpharmaceutical interventions: Determinants of dynamic compliance and behavioral shifts
pmc-11648666.creator: Alina Glaubitz, Feng Fu
pmc-11648666.description: SignificanceThe effectiveness of nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPI) depends on widespread compliance, without which infection waves can surge, driven by pathogen evolution and changing public vigilance. Here, we reveal that bottom–up adherence to NPI measures is dynamic and varies according to context, leading to intricate temporal changes in preferences between NPI measures or inaction through an ongoing epidemic.

pmc-11713676.title: Detecting Undue Harm Arising From Elder Abuse Screening: Innovative Methods from the EASI‐ltc© Pilot Study
pmc-11713676.creator: Machelle Wilchesky, Stephanie A. Ballard
pmc-11713676.description: BackgroundScreening for elder abuse can cause victims to experience feelings of unpleasantness and/or relive painful memories which can be an ethical concern. Ensuring the safety of all participants/users, in our case long‐term care (LTC) residents, is of the utmost importance.

pmc-13223348.title: Listeria Genome Identification Using DNABERT Embedding With LightGBM and SHAP-Based Explainable Classification
pmc-13223348.creator: Sajeev Ram Arumugam, Ananth J P, Sankar Ganesh Karuppasamy, V Senthil Murugan, Wulfran Fendzi Mbasso, Ambe Harrison
pmc-13223348.description: Prompt and accurate identification of Listeria monocytogenes at the whole-genome level is essential for food safety surveillance and outbreak prevention, yet existing culture-based, PCR, and next-generation sequencing (NGS) workflows are either slow, labor-intensive, or rely on opaque machine learning models with limited interpretability.

pmc-13375339.title: The digital bioeconomy: microbiomes as a stress test for global digital sequence information governance
pmc-13375339.creator: Pierre-Mathieu Pélissier, Indré Karciauskaité, Tanja Kostic, Emmanuelle Maguin, Angela Sessitsch, Kosuke Shiraishi
pmc-13375339.description: Digital sequence information governance has entered a high-stakes implementation era. The Convention on Biological Diversity’s ‘Cali Fund’ is operationalised as the financial engine of its multilateral mechanism (MLM), with similar frameworks under negotiation across other international ocean and agricultural treaties. However, because microorganisms and their functional clusters transcend national borders, traditional bilateral mechanisms are difficult to implement.

uslaw-usc-t42-s5814.title: 42 U.S.C. § 5814 — Abolition and transfers
uslaw-usc-t42-s5814.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s5814.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 73 (Development Of Energy Sources); Subchapter I (Energy Research And Development Administration). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Abolition of Atomic Energy Commission The Atomic Energy Commission is hereby abolished. Sections 2031 and 2032 of this title are repealed. (b) Transfer or lapse of functions of Atomic Energy Commission All other.
